title: You Got a Raise... So Why Are You Still Broke?

blocks.text: You got a raise. Why are you still broke?
blocks.visual: Close-up on the edge of a pay stub showing a highlighted 'Net Pay' line.

blocks.text: First thing people do is upgrade lifestyle instantly, new phone or dinners every weekend.
blocks.visual: Medium shot of a hand tapping 'Buy' on a smartphone checkout screen with a new gadget image.

blocks.text: Second trap is 'hidden recurring costs', streaming, subscriptions, higher bills by habit.
blocks.visual: Insert, close shot of several app subscription icons stacked, a finger hovering over a credit card.

blocks.text: Imagine this, you get more salary and your rent or lifestyle doesn't change, yet your free cash shrinks.
blocks.visual: Wide shot of a small apartment living room, a single lamp on, an empty wallet on the table.

blocks.text: Big escalation, debt quietly grows. People use cards to bridge between higher lifestyle and payday.
blocks.visual: Medium shot of a hand sliding a credit card into a reader, a balance alert glowing on phone screen.

blocks.text: Small detail most miss, paycheck illusions. Taxes, retirement contributions, and benefits can cut take-home pay.
blocks.visual: Insert, close-up of a payroll breakdown on screen showing labeled deductions (Taxes, 401k, Insurance).

blocks.text: Pattern interrupt, some people actually save more after a raise. What's different is one habit.
blocks.visual: Close-up on two jars labeled 'Spend' and 'Save' as one hand moves a bill into 'Save'.

blocks.text: Concrete trick used: 'pay yourself first', automatically move a share of the raise to savings before spending.
blocks.visual: POV shot looking down at a phone confirming an automatic transfer labeled 'Emergency fund'.

blocks.text: Here's a simple example, if you increase your saving share of the raise to just a portion, your free cash still covers upgrades.
blocks.visual: Insert, close shot of calculator showing an example labeled 'Example, hypothetical split' (no numbers shown in narration).

blocks.text: Reveal, the real reason you're broke after a raise is not the raise. It's the shift in choices and invisible commitments.
blocks.visual: Wide shot of the same apartment now with visible bills on table and a single coin in the wallet.

blocks.text: Resolution, make one rule. Automate a part of every raise to savings or debt paydown, then enjoy the rest guilt-free.
blocks.visual: Medium shot of a phone setting an recurring transfer labeled 'Raise → Savings' and a checkmark appearing.

blocks.text: Would you automate part of your raise or spend it all?
blocks.visual: Close-up on two labeled jars 'Automate' and 'Spend', camera centered between them.

contentStrategy.audiencePromise: Understand why a raise doesn't solve money stress and get a simple rule to change it.
contentStrategy.coreQuestion: Why does a raise often leave you with no more free cash?
contentStrategy.viewerProblem: You earn more but your spending and hidden costs rise, so you feel no better off.
contentStrategy.payoff: Automate a portion of any raise to savings or debt paydown first, then spend the rest. Example placeholders shown as $Saved and $Spent in visuals.
contentStrategy.curiosityMechanism: Start with the surprising fact, then show the exact small choices that undo a raise and a concrete automated fix.
contentStrategy.hookText: You got a raise. Why are you still broke?
